structural: The requirement prescribes structure: a `#[non_exhaustive]` struct with named public fields and types (`model: String`, `endpoint: Option<String>`, `api_key_env: Option<String>`, `api_key: Option<SecretString>`, `options: BTreeMap<String, OptionValue>`). It also prescribes five builder-style signatures and the trait implementations Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq and Serialize. Changing any of these would violate the text, so they are structural obligations. All of them map to the supplied roots:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs#struct[OllamaConfig]` declares `#[non_exhaustive]` and the exact fields and types. Its `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]` supplies all five required trait implementations. The serde attributes (`default`, `skip_serializing_if`, `deny_unknown_fields`) are extra serialized-form details that the text does not forbid.
- `impl[OllamaConfig]#1/fn[new]` has the signature `new(model: String) -> Self`. It sets `model` and leaves the optional fields `None` and `options` empty.
- `fn[endpoint]`, `fn[api_key_env]` and `fn[api_key]` each take `self` by value plus the prescribed argument type, set the corresponding field to `Some(..)`, and return `Self`.
- `fn[option]` takes `(self, key: String, value: OptionValue) -> Self` and inserts into the `options` map.

Each root carries an `{impl}` reference to `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig`. No other structural obligation is missing evidence. The sentence about how the endpoint, credentials and options configure requests is behavioral, so it is outside this structural review.

behavioral: The reviewed tests adequately cover the observable obligations of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig`. I did not read the implementation source.

The requirement's obligations and the tests that cover them:

- **Constructor and builders.** `new(model)` sets only `model`, and each builder sets only its field.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs#mod[tests]/fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` checks that `OllamaConfig::new("ollama-model")` serializes to `{"model":"ollama-model"}`. This also shows that unset `Option` fields are omitted and `options` is empty.
  - The same test applies `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key` and `option`, then asserts the exact serialized object.
  - It calls `option` with key "a" twice, giving the second call the value 2. The assertion `"options":{"a":2,"b":true}` confirms the second value replaces the first and the other keys are kept.

- **Serialize and Deserialize.** `fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` deserializes an Ollama config with `api_key_env` and nested float options, then re-serializes it. It asserts the result equals the input value. It also round-trips through a JSON string and asserts `config == copy`, which exercises `PartialEq` for configs that include an `OllamaConfig`.

- **Configuring requests to the server.** `endpoint`, `api_key`, `api_key_env` and `options` are the request-configuration fields.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_ollama_backend_delivers_tools_and_results_over_native_chat]` runs a real local HTTP server and gives the config `model`, `endpoint`, `api_key` and `options`.
  - It asserts the request goes to the supplied endpoint at `POST /api/chat`. It also asserts the `Authorization: Bearer local-ollama-key` header, `model == "local-ollama"`, and `options.num_predict == 256`.
  - `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` covers the `api_key_env` path. A missing environment variable gives an error that names the variable. An explicit `api_key` resolves to its value. The default endpoint resolves to `http://localhost:11434`, and no key resolves to `None`. Invalid float options (NaN, infinity) are rejected by `options_json`.

- **Public shape.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory against the specification.

- **`Clone` and `Debug`.** These are derive-style trait declarations with no stated behavior beyond their presence. They have no independent observable obligation, so no further test is needed.

I found no unacknowledged gaps.

text: `model` names the model on the Ollama server. The endpoint, credentials, and inference options configure requests to that server.
pub fn endpoint(self, endpoint: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key_env(self, api_key_env: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key(self, api_key: SecretString) -> Self;
pub fn option(self, key: String, value: OptionValue) -> Self;
